colorPrompt: Compose one children's book picture from the element pictures. Picture 1 is the classroom: a wooden floor with a red rug, bookshelves, a table, and a cream wall with dark-brown timber beams. Use its walls, floor, and rug as the background and keep the same classroom, framed closer with a low camera. Picture 2 shows four approved children from left to right: Pat, May, Sam, and Mia. Picture 3 shows from left to right: the boy Ben, the girl Nan, the grown woman Teacher Kim, and a puppy (the puppy must NOT appear in this picture). Copy each person exactly as shown, with the same hair, face, and clothes. Keep the soft, round, bright 3D render look of the pictures, not a 2D drawing and no outlines. The people: Pat: short messy black hair with a fringe and a few small tufts on top, big brown eyes, a small smile, a green T-shirt, brown cargo shorts, brown sandals (without the teddy bear); May: black hair with a fringe and one long ponytail at the side with a small yellow star hair clip, big brown eyes, a small smile, a yellow T-shirt, a blue pleated skirt, white socks, white sneakers; Sam: short brown hair with a side-swept fringe, big brown eyes, a big open-mouth smile, a red T-shirt with two white stripes, blue shorts, blue shoes; Mia: light-brown shoulder-length hair with a small pink bow on the side, big brown eyes, an open-mouth smile, a pink T-shirt, blue denim overalls, white shoes; Ben: short messy light-brown hair, big brown eyes, a big open-mouth smile, a light-blue T-shirt, dark-blue shorts, grey sneakers; Nan: black-brown hair in two buns with red hair ties, large dark-brown eyes, a small smile, an orange T-shirt with a white star, red shorts, white sneakers; Teacher Kim: a grown woman, about one and a half times as tall as the children, with medium-length dark-brown hair in a low ponytail, a soft green cardigan over a cream blouse, navy trousers, brown flat shoes, a gentle smile. The picture: exactly seven people, no dog. Teacher Kim kneels on the rug at the left of the picture, so that her face is at the children's eye level, and waves hello with her raised hand, open, with a gentle smile, looking at the children. The six children sit close together on the red rug at the middle and the right of the picture, in two rows (three in front, three behind), all facing the camera and Teacher Kim, and all wave back with one raised open hand and a happy open-mouth smile. Everyone is seen full-body or sitting, large enough that every face is clear. Hands are small, chubby child hands with five clear short fingers and a thumb when open, never fists unless stated. A hand that reaches toward the camera looks larger because of perspective; that is correct. Clean eye corners with no skin flaps, no streak on the forehead, and no marks on the face. Rendering errors to NOT copy from the character pictures: a tiny dark tick mark or pale skin flap at the outer corner of an eye (the corner next to the ear), and a faint pale crease on a forehead. Each eye ends in a smooth, rounded corner. Nan alone keeps one short, thick, curved eyelash flick at each outer eye corner. The page text is "Hello, I am your teacher." and is context only: do not draw any text. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no writing on any picture or sign. The picture is for young children and is rated G.
linePrompt: Picture 1 is a 3D-rendered children's book picture. Convert picture 1 to line art for a student book: thick, even black lines (about three times a normal outline), simple closed shapes that a 5-year-old can color, on pure white. No blush circles, no eyelash ticks, no hair strands, no shading, no gray, no texture lines, no text. Keep every shape in the same place and the same size. Draw each eye as a closed outline with a big solid black pupil (a filled black circle) inside it. Draw the mouth exactly as in picture 1: an open mouth stays an open mouth drawn as a closed outline, and a closed smile stays one curve. Keep all seven people, the rug, and the floor as thick, closed outlines. Every person keeps a face with two eyes with pupils and a mouth. Teacher Kim keeps her ponytail as one closed shape. Draw each head of hair as one closed shape. Simplify the background: draw only a few large, simple, closed shapes. No small details, no grass blades, no small leaves, no hatching, no tick marks, no wood grain lines. Every shape is closed with one thick line. Draw the bookshelves as a few big plain rectangles with no books. Draw the rug as one plain closed shape with no fringe, no dotted line, no dashed line, and no tick marks anywhere. Draw no diamond pattern on the rug. The outline of each object (a branch, a leaf cluster, a bag, a table, a tree) is one closed shape that does not run into a hill line or a floor line. Use few background shapes and no bushes or hills that are not needed.
